An Earth descent.

The scene, the choices, and the revision that shaped it.

OverviewConstructionAI & human choicesRevision & limitsTry it

Web experience · Tested 26 September 2026

An Earth descent for Azivor

Scroll the homepage and the view moves from space toward clouds and a lighter sky. This scene gives the site its opening rhythm.

01 / Construction

From orbit to sky.

What was built

A scroll-driven scene with a textured spherical Earth, layered clouds, a sparse star field, and a gradual transition into the page content. It is rendered in a WebGL canvas; the page has a visual fallback and reduced-motion layout.

How it worked

Scroll position controls the camera approach and the surrounding color. The globe and cloud layers use image textures, while the shader draws depth and atmosphere. The text and navigation remain HTML above the canvas.

02 / Attribution

The tools. The choices.

What AI did

AI-generated visual studies helped explore the Earth and cloud direction. They were references for the look; the live scene is implemented as code and checked in the browser.

What required human judgment

Choosing the pace of descent, keeping the sky readable behind the headline, and deciding when the scene should give way to actual information on the page.

03 / Reflection

What held up.

Let the Earth hide the headline.

Revision record · 27 September 2026

Before
The opening copy moved upward and faded out within the first fifth of the descent.
The decision
Keep the copy still. Let the globe’s curved edge explain why it disappears.
After
The text stays in place and is progressively covered by the Earth. Covered controls leave keyboard navigation; reduced-motion and fallback views keep the copy visible.
Check it yourself
Scroll the homepage and watch the headline meet the globe’s edge. Compare the behavior with the recorded source change.
View the live descentInspect the recorded revision

This records a design change, not a measured improvement in usability or graphics performance.

What worked and what did not

The Earth sequence gave the site a distinct opening. Early versions left too much empty blue space and ended too abruptly; the transition and middle of the journey needed more attention. The scene remains a visual study, and its effect on loading speed has not been established.
